about: Generator-side notes on must_show items (not part of the rule set). conditional: whether the item applies in some files only; applies_when: a condition over designed fact states that makes a conditional item required (if it does not hold, the item does not apply and is left out); checkable_as: what a document must literally contain for the item to count as shown, passed to the writer and to the blind checker; observed: the round-1 blind-check mismatch that led to the entry; rule_set_wording: why the item's own wording is a problem, for the planner to raise with the rule set (absent where the wording is fine).

items.item: a statement of the form used: the printed title of the form approved by the canton, or a sentence on the notice that it is or is not given on that form; for an increase the file states is a graduated-rent step, a written notice suffices instead (art. 269d para. 5)
items.checkable_as: The notice itself says whether it is made on the official form approved by the canton: the printed title of that form, or an explicit sentence that the official form is used or enclosed, or that it is not. A plain letter that is silent about any form does not show this item. Exception: where the file states that the increase is a graduated-rent step, any written notice shows this item (art. 269d para. 5).
items.rule_set_wording: A 'whether ...' item is shown by every document (silence reads as 'no'), so an insufficient copy cannot be told from a sufficient one; better: 'the official cantonal form, or a statement that it is not used'.
items.revision_3: Revision 3 (second look, 2026-11-12): graduated-rent exception added, as the second reader worded it (R2-6).

items.item: Only if the file states that the increase applies an index clause: the old and the new index value. Otherwise this item does not apply.
items.checkable_as: Two index values, old and new, with the index named (for example 'consumer price index 104.2 -> 106.9').
items.observed: ten_efa24ba18ce3: designed sufficient (item treated as optional), read missing because the file states an index clause
items.rule_set_wording: The condition is part of the item; it belongs in needed_when-style data, not in the content list.

items.item: Only if the file states that the landlord gave notice of termination together with the rent increase: the notice or threat of termination in the increase notice or its covering letter. Otherwise this item does not apply.
items.checkable_as: The threat or notice of termination, in the notice or its covering letter.

items.item: Only if the file states that the increase is a graduated-rent step or applies an index clause: the lease clause that fixes the graduated steps or links the rent to an index. Otherwise this item does not apply.
items.checkable_as: The clause that fixes the graduated steps or links the rent to an index.

items.item: Only if the file states that the landlord terminated because rent or accessory charges were not paid within a payment time limit (art. 257d): the copy of that payment time limit served separately on the spouse or registered partner. Otherwise this item does not apply.
the date on which the claims were brought before the conciliation authority, or a sentence that they have not yet been brought
items.checkable_as: A date on which the claims were filed with the conciliation authority, or an explicit statement that they have not yet been filed.

items.item: Only if the file states that the tenant's claims were brought before a conciliation authority or a court: the conciliation or court documents on those claims. Otherwise this item does not apply.
